question: Which two groups combine to form the carboxyl group found in organic acids?
explanation: The carboxyl group is formed when a carbonyl group and a hydroxyl group are attached to the same carbon atom. [learn more](BMP113_U4_T5#BMP113_U4_T5_h1)

question: How do the oxygen atoms affect electron density within a carboxyl group?

options.A: Electron density is pulled away from the central carbon and hydrogen
options.B: Electron density remains evenly distributed across all atoms
options.C: Electron density concentrates only around the double-bonded oxygen
options.D: Electron density is pushed entirely toward the hydrocarbon chain

explanation: The electronegative oxygen atoms draw electron density away, which weakens the O-H bond and facilitates proton release. [learn more](BMP113_U4_T5#BMP113_U4_T5_h1)

question: What standard suffix is used when naming a straight-chain carboxylic acid?
explanation: IUPAC naming conventions require replacing the terminal 'e' of the parent alkane with the suffix -oic acid. [learn more](BMP113_U4_T5#BMP113_U4_T5_h2)

question: Which position number does the carboxyl carbon always receive on the carbon chain during naming?
explanation: The carbon atom belonging to the carboxyl group holds the highest priority and is designated as carbon number one. [learn more](BMP113_U4_T5#BMP113_U4_T5_h2)

question: Why do carboxylic acids have higher boiling points than similarly sized alcohols?

options.A: They contain ionic bonds instead of traditional covalent bonds
options.B: Their carbon chains are much heavier than those of standard alcohols
options.C: Their double-bonded oxygens prevent any intermolecular movement
options.D: They form stable cyclic dimers through two hydrogen bonds at the same time

explanation: The ability to form robust double hydrogen-bonded dimers requires more thermal energy to break apart, raising the boiling point. [learn more](BMP113_U4_T5#BMP113_U4_T5_h3)

question: Which of the following carboxylic acids is expected to be the least soluble in water?

options.A: Ethanoic acid with a two-carbon chain
options.B: Methanoic acid with a one-carbon chain
options.C: Propanoic acid with a three-carbon chain
options.D: Decanoic acid with a ten-carbon chain

explanation: As the non-polar hydrocarbon chain lengthens, the hydrophobic property overpowers the polar carboxyl group, reducing water solubility. [learn more](BMP113_U4_T5#BMP113_U4_T5_h3)

question: What is the name of the negatively charged ion formed when a carboxylic acid loses a proton?
explanation: Deprotonation of a carboxylic acid yields a carboxylate ion along with a hydronium ion. [learn more](BMP113_U4_T5#BMP113_U4_T5_h4)

question: How does resonance stabilization affect the strength of a carboxylic acid?

options.A: It prevents the molecule from ionizing in aqueous solutions
options.B: It changes the boiling point without altering acid dissociation
options.C: It makes the acid stronger by stabilizing the resulting negative charge
options.D: It makes the acid weaker by trapping the proton on the oxygen atom

explanation: Sharing the negative charge across multiple oxygen atoms stabilizes the conjugate base, encouraging acid dissociation. [learn more](BMP113_U4_T5#BMP113_U4_T5_h4)

question: What two starting materials are needed to make an ester in a classic Fischer esterification reaction?
explanation: Esterification combines a carboxylic acid and an alcohol, typically heated with an acid catalyst. [learn more](BMP113_U4_T5#BMP113_U4_T5_h5)

question: What organic product is formed when a carboxylic acid is completely reduced using lithium aluminum hydride?
explanation: Powerful reducing agents like lithium aluminum hydride reduce carboxylic acids all the way down to primary alcohols. [learn more](BMP113_U4_T5#BMP113_U4_T5_h5)

question: Which common household medication is a derivative of a carboxylic acid?
explanation: Aspirin, chemically known as acetylsalicylic acid, contains a carboxylic acid group that contributes to its therapeutic actions. [learn more](BMP113_U4_T5#BMP113_U4_T5_h6)

question: Why is knowing the properties of carboxylic acids clinically relevant for healthcare professionals?

options.A: It helps explain drug solubility, ionization, and how agents behave in body fluids
options.B: It determines the exact expiration date of liquid suspension drugs
options.C: It prevents allergic reactions from occurring during intravenous therapy
options.D: It allows clinicians to synthesize new antibiotics directly at the bedside

explanation: Ionization states of carboxylic acid drugs directly influence how they dissolve, absorb, and transport across biological membranes. [learn more](BMP113_U4_T5#BMP113_U4_T5_h6)
